metadata.title: B1: Transparency Reform
metadata.description: The Watergate-era reform pattern. Perceived corruption mobilizes reform movements, which pass disclosure laws, which produce visibility, which produces accountability, which rebuilds trust — closing the balancing loop.
metadata.author: US Government Intelligent Textbook

nodes.label: Public Perception of Corruption
nodes.description: Citizens' belief that officials trade favors for money. The trigger that starts the loop.

nodes.label: Demand for Reform
nodes.description: Sustained public pressure — petitions, protests, reform candidates — calling for ethics laws.

nodes.label: Transparency Laws
nodes.description: FECA, FOIA, BCRA, HONEST Leadership Act — statutes requiring disclosure of money and meetings.

nodes.label: Visibility of Political Funding
nodes.description: How easy it is to find out who is paying for political messages and advocacy.

nodes.label: Institutional Accountability
nodes.description: Visible consequences — resignations, prosecutions, electoral defeats — when officials betray public trust.

nodes.label: Trust In Government
nodes.description: The percentage of citizens who say they trust the federal government to do what is right.

edges.description: Sustained reform pressure passes disclosure and ethics legislation.
Disclosure laws let journalists and watchdogs see the money.
Visible misconduct produces resignations, prosecutions, electoral defeats.
Restored trust reduces perceived corruption — closing the balancing loop.

loops.label: B1: Transparency Reform
loops.description: The Watergate-era reform pattern (1972–1978 produced the Ethics in Government Act).
